title: Digital Product Passport — EU 2024/1781 ESPR + 2023/1542 Battery + GS1 Digital Link + NTAG 424 DNA
summary: Digital Product Passports (DPP) are becoming mandatory in the EU for textiles, batteries, electronics and other product categories starting 2027 under EU Regulation 2024/1781 (ESPR) plus the earlier 2023/1542 Batteries Regulation. NFC tags embedded in products provide a tap-to-access digital passport containing material composition, manufacturing origin, carbon footprint, repairability information and recycling instructions, carried as GS1 Digital Link 1.3 (ISO/IEC 18975:2023) URLs and (where authentication is required) signed with NTAG 424 DNA SUN / CMAC. Proud Tek supplies the NFC tags and RFID labels that brands need to implement DPP compliance while enhancing consumer engagement. Implementation aligns with the CIRPASS-2 reference architecture and the EU Battery Pass (BatteryPassport.org) data model.
heroPoints: EU regulation compliance: meet the EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) requirements for machine-readable product information accessible to consumers, recyclers and authorities.
Tap-to-access: consumers, retailers and recycling facilities tap their smartphone on the NFC tag to access the complete digital product passport via a web interface, no app required.
Secure and tamper-proof. NFC tags with NTAG 424 DNA provide cryptographic authentication ensuring the passport data has not been altered or the tag transplanted from another product.

brief.label: Regulatory phase-in calendar — what triggers each product group
items: Batteries — EU 2023/1542 Battery Passport effective 18 February 2027 for industrial / EV / LMT batteries ≥2 kWh.
Textiles + apparel + footwear — EU 2024/1781 ESPR delegated act expected 2026; mandatory DPP from 2027.
Electronics + ICT consumer goods — phased delegated acts 2027–2029 covering smartphones, displays, household appliances.
Construction products + furniture — DPP-aligned obligations from 2028 onward under construction-products regulation revision.
Iron + steel + aluminium + chemicals + plastics — industrial DPP under separate ESPR working plan.
Tyres — EU 2020/740 EPREL + ESPR convergence; tyre-passport pilot 2026.

brief.label: Mandatory passport content — eight ESPR data buckets
items: Material composition with percentage breakdown including recycled content, hazardous substances (REACH SVHC), and SCIP-database alignment.
Manufacturing origin: country / facility / supplier hierarchy of key components and raw materials, mapped to GS1 GLN.
Environmental footprint: carbon (GHG kgCO2e), water, energy and PEF (Product Environmental Footprint) per Commission Recommendation 2021/2279.
Durability + repairability: expected lifespan, repair instructions, spare-part availability index, repairability score per JRC framework.
End-of-life routing: WEEE / battery / textile / packaging take-back instructions, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme.
Compliance documentation: CE marking + EU declaration of conformity + applicable harmonised standards + notified-body number.
Repair, spare-parts and software-update history (electronics) per EU Right-to-Repair Directive 2024/1799.
Substance-of-Concern declarations (REACH Article 33) — hazardous substances above 0.1 % w/w.

brief.label: Stakeholder access tiers — who sees what under DPP
items: Consumer tier (public): brand + product + composition + care + repair + recycling — accessible via tap with no authentication.
Repair-network tier: spare-part SKUs + service-procedure access + warranty validation — authenticated via service-account.
Recycler tier: disassembly instructions + hazardous-substance map + material recovery routing — accessible to certified recyclers.
Authority tier (Market Surveillance + Customs): declaration-of-conformity + technical-documentation pointer + IPR enforcement — full audit access.
B2B / supply-chain tier: PEF + Scope-3 emissions + supplier ESG + contract-compliance — partner-authenticated.

brief.label: NFC chip choice — when 424 DNA vs NTAG21x is right
items: NTAG 424 DNA SUN baseline — required when authentication-grade trust is needed (luxury / regulated / brand-protected).
NTAG 424 DNA TagTamper — when seal-broken detection adds value (cosmetics, spirits, premium electronics, refurbished goods).
NTAG 213/215/216 with Originality Signature — sufficient when DPP is open-data + database-backed (low-risk product groups).
ICODE DNA — HF longer-range alternative for warehouse / logistics DPP scanning where consumer tap is secondary.
MIFARE DESFire EV3 — multi-application file structure for products combining DPP + access + payment / loyalty.

brief.label: Data carrier choice — NFC + QR + RFID hybrid
items: NFC primary, QR backup — luxury + premium textiles where consumer tap-to-verify is the primary UX.
QR primary, NFC optional — lower-cost mass-market FMCG where camera-scan is the established consumer behaviour.
UHF RFID + NFC — pallet / case + item-level convergence for warehouse logistics + consumer touchpoints.
GS1 Digital Link 1.3 (ISO/IEC 18975:2023) — required URL structure for any data carrier; resolvable to product master record.
DataMatrix + GS1 — pharmaceutical (DSCSA / EU FMD) DPP convergence path.

brief.label: Backend / DPP-as-a-service platform ecosystem
items: EVRYTHNG (now atma.io by Avery Dennison) — apparel + textiles digital-twin + DPP at scale; Inditex / Kering / PVH deployments.
TrusTrace — supply-chain transparency + DPP for textiles + leather goods.
EON — DPP + circularity passport for fashion + retail + outdoor brands.
Authena — luxury + fashion DPP combined with anti-counterfeit authentication.
Spherity (Decentralised Identifiers + Verifiable Credentials) — pharma + battery DPP with EU eIDAS-2 alignment.
Adena, Origyn, Scantrust — cross-vertical DPP + authentication backend partners.
Custom enterprise build — using SAP Sustainability Footprint + Salesforce Net Zero Cloud + AWS / Azure verification microservices.

brief.label: Battery Passport (EU 2023/1542) detail
items: In scope: industrial batteries >2 kWh + LMT batteries >2 kWh + EV batteries — effective 18 February 2027.
Mandatory data: chemistry + capacity + State-of-Health (SoH) + Carbon Footprint (CFB) + recycled-content quotas + supply-chain due diligence.
Identifier: GS1 GTIN + serial — encoded as GS1 Digital Link URL on QR + NFC + UHF RFID per battery vendor preference.
Custodianship: economic operator placing on market; passport lives in EU registry with decentralised registries permitted.
Reference architecture: Battery Pass consortium (BMW, BASF, Volkswagen, Umicore, Spherity) + CIRPASS-2 alignment.

brief.label: Textile + apparel DPP — early-mover deep dive
items: Scope: garments + footwear + home textiles placed on EU market; phase-in 2027–2028 per delegated act.
Identifier: GS1 GTIN + serial recommended; GS1 Digital Link 1.3 URL carried by NFC inlay sewn into care label or hang-tag.
Mandatory data: fibre composition + recycled content + country-of-origin + care instructions + repair / take-back.
Voluntary attributes: PEF Apparel category + ZDHC chemistry + B-corp / Fair Trade / Cradle-to-Cradle certifications.
Pilot deployments: H&M, Inditex, Decathlon, VF Corp, Patagonia, Allbirds — already running DPP MVPs at SKU level.

brief.label: CIRPASS-2 reference architecture + EU Single Digital Gateway
items: CIRPASS-2 (EU Horizon Europe-funded, 2023–2025) — pre-deployment DPP architecture coordination project.
Decentralised Identifiers (DIDs) + Verifiable Credentials (VCs) — W3C-aligned trust layer for cross-registry interoperability.
Persistent identifiers: GS1 GTIN + ISBN + GS1 GLN + economic-operator EORI + product-passport-specific UUID.
Resolver layer: GS1 Resolver + brand-owned resolvers + EU registry — multi-tier resolution per ISO/IEC 18975 informative annex.
EU Single Digital Gateway compliance — DPP-API consumed by Member State market-surveillance authorities.

brief.label: Implementation programme economics + governance
items: Tag BOM: NTAG 424 DNA $0.20–$0.60; NTAG213 $0.05–$0.15; UHF RFID $0.04–$0.12 — at 100k+ volume.
Backend SaaS: $0.10–$1.00 per product per year for DPP-as-a-service tier (atma.io / TrusTrace / EON / Authena).
Data-readiness investment: bills-of-material + supplier ESG + PEF calculation + chemistry-disclosure datasets — typically 12–24 months pre-launch effort.
Governance: cross-functional sponsor (CSO / CCO + supply chain + IT + legal + compliance + brand-marketing).
Metrics: SKU-coverage % + tag-deployment % + tap-rate per SKU + repair-rate uplift + recycling-rate uplift + counterfeit-detection contribution.

sections.title: What the EU Digital Product Passport requires
bullets: Material composition: detailed information about materials used in the product, including percentage of recycled content, hazardous substances and material sourcing.
Manufacturing origin: supply chain transparency showing where the product was manufactured, assembled and the origin of key components and raw materials.
Environmental footprint: carbon footprint, water usage, energy consumption and other environmental impact metrics for the product's lifecycle.
Durability and repairability: expected product lifespan, repair instructions, spare part availability and repairability score.
End-of-life instructions. Recycling guidelines, disassembly instructions, material recovery information and collection point locations for proper disposal.

Machine-readable format: the passport must be accessible via a machine-readable data carrier (QR code, NFC tag, or RFID) linked to a unique product identifier in a centralized or decentralized data system.

comparePanel.afterHeading: NFC + GS1 Digital Link 1.3 + DPP backend (regulation-ready)
before: Single-payload QR encoding text or PDF link — opaque content, hard to update post-shipment.
Product attributes maintained in disconnected spreadsheets per business unit — version drift between spec, marketing and compliance.
No authentication — counterfeit product with cloned QR passes consumer scrutiny.
Camera scan UX — failure rates 5–15 % depending on lighting + curvature + print quality.
No stakeholder-tier differentiation — consumer / authority / recycler all see the same view.
Audit trail: none at the product level; difficult to produce compliance evidence for regulators.
after: GS1 Digital Link URL resolves dynamically to current passport — content updateable post-shipment without re-tagging.
Single source of truth in DPP backend (atma.io / TrusTrace / EON / Authena) — fed by SAP / Salesforce / supplier portals.
NTAG 424 DNA SUN authentication — every tap signed; counterfeit cloned tag detected server-side.
Tap UX — iPhone XS+ background tag reading; Android NDEF dispatch; success rate 98 %+ in normal use.
Stakeholder-tier resolution — consumer / repair-network / recycler / authority each see passport view appropriate to credentials.
Audit trail per product unit — every tap logged; defensible compliance evidence for EU market-surveillance + customs.

sections.title: Why NFC is the ideal technology for Digital Product Passports
bullets: Premium consumer interaction: a smartphone tap is more intuitive and premium-feeling than pointing a camera at a QR code, aligning with the brand experience expectations of luxury, fashion and premium product categories.
Authentication built-in: NTAG 424 DNA provides cryptographic verification alongside the DPP data, confirming both product authenticity and passport data integrity in a single tap.
Tamper evidence: NFC tags with tamper-detect features confirm the passport is associated with the original product and has not been transplanted from another item.
Durable lifecycle: NFC tags embedded in products survive the product's entire useful life, remaining readable for years (no battery, no degradation) unlike printed QR codes that fade and scratch.

Multi-stakeholder access (consumers see product information and care instructions; recyclers see material composition and disassembly guides; authorities see compliance data and supply chain documentation) all from the same tag tap.

dataHighlight.heading: DPP programme — 2026 baseline metrics under ESPR + Battery Regulation
dataHighlight.text: ESPR establishes Digital Product Passport for product groups including textiles, electronics, furniture, batteries from 2027 onward. 18 Feb 2027 — EU 2023/1542 Battery Passport effective date for industrial + LMT + EV batteries ≥2 kWh. ISO/IEC 18975:2023 — GS1 Digital Link 1.3 — required web-resolvable URI carried by NFC / QR / UHF RFID across all DPP product groups. $0.20–$0.60 — NTAG 424 DNA tag BOM at 100k+ volume; $0.05–$0.15 for NTAG213 baseline; $0.04–$0.12 for UHF RFID alternative. ≥2 kWh — Threshold for batteries falling under EU 2023/1542 Battery Passport — covers EV + e-bike + e-scooter + grid-scale storage. iPhone XS+ — Background tag reading enabled by default since iOS 14; consumer DPP access requires no app download on iOS or Android.

timeline.title: DPP implementation programme — design through compliance go-live

items.text: Map product portfolio against ESPR + 2023/1542 Battery Regulation + sector-specific delegated acts. Identify in-scope SKUs by product group + EU market exposure. Convene cross-functional sponsor team (CSO / CCO + supply chain + IT + legal + compliance + brand-marketing). Define SKU-level DPP-readiness scorecard.
items.label: Quarter 1 — Regulatory scoping and stakeholder alignment

items.text: Inventory existing data sources: PLM (Centric / FlexPLM / Bamboo Rose) + ERP (SAP / Oracle / Microsoft Dynamics) + supplier portals + chemistry / REACH / SCIP databases + LCA / PEF tools. Gap-fill: bill-of-material rolled up to component level + supplier ESG attestation + carbon-footprint per SKU + repairability score.
items.label: Quarter 2 — Data-readiness inventory and gap analysis

items.text: Select DPP-as-a-service partner (atma.io / TrusTrace / EON / Authena / Spherity) or commit to custom enterprise build. Define API contracts to PLM / ERP / supplier portals. Design GS1 Digital Link URL structure + resolver topology + DID / VC trust layer per CIRPASS-2 reference architecture.
items.label: Quarter 3 — Backend platform selection and integration design

items.text: Choose NFC chip per product group: NTAG 424 DNA SUN for authentication-grade categories (luxury / regulated / premium); NTAG21x for low-risk open-data DPP. Decide form factor: care-label inlay (textiles), cap-seal (cosmetics + spirits), embedded inlay (electronics + leather), bottle-neck wrap (batteries + chemicals). Validate tap-through-package read range.
items.label: Quarter 4 — Tag-spec selection and form-factor lock-in

items.text: Launch pilot on representative cohort (1 luxury textile + 1 mass-market apparel + 1 EV battery + 1 cosmetic + 1 electronics). Validate end-to-end: SKU → tag encode → embed → consumer tap → backend verify → multi-tier passport view → analytics dashboard. Collect tap-rate + scan-failure + consumer-feedback metrics.
items.label: Quarter 5 — Pilot SKU launch on 5–20 product lines

items.text: Scale tag procurement to full 2027 production volume. Onboard suppliers to data-feed contracts. Train repair-network + recycler-network on stakeholder-tier authentication. Train customer-service + brand-marketing teams on tap-failure + counterfeit escalation workflow.
items.label: Quarter 6 — Pre-2027 production-ramp and supplier onboarding

items.text: Battery Passport effective 18 February 2027 for industrial / EV / LMT batteries ≥2 kWh — first product group requiring live DPP. Submit DPP API to EU Member State market-surveillance registries. Begin consumer-facing tap-to-verify campaign. Monitor tap-failure + cross-border product-flow + customs IPR enforcement.
items.label: Q1 2027 — Compliance go-live for first product group (batteries 18 Feb 2027)

items.text: Programme references draw from luxury-brands, eu-compliance, brand-protection, retail-apparel and pharmaceutical estates, with periodic compliance reviews, refresh-cycle planning and supplier-onboarding gates customised per vertical. quarterly DPP audit + delegated-act monitoring (textiles 2027, electronics 2028, construction 2028+, furniture 2028+); annual platform refresh + key-vault rotation; CIRPASS-2 + EU Single Digital Gateway alignment review; Member-State authority registry reconciliation; expansion of programme scope to additional product groups as ESPR delegated acts publish.

faq.question: When do Digital Product Passport requirements take effect?
faq.answer: The EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) was adopted in 2024, with DPP requirements phasing in by product category: batteries (18 February 2027 under EU 2023/1542), textiles (2027 under ESPR delegated act), electronics and ICT (2028-2029), with additional categories including furniture, construction and chemicals following. Brands should begin implementation now to be ready for compliance deadlines and to gain early-mover advantage with sustainability-conscious consumers.

faq.question: Can the same NFC tag serve as both DPP carrier and anti-counterfeit device?
faq.answer: Yes. NTAG 424 DNA tags combine secure data storage (for DPP information or cloud links via GS1 Digital Link 1.3 URL) with cryptographic authentication (AES-128 SUN / CMAC for anti-counterfeiting). A single tap verifies the product is genuine and provides access to the complete digital product passport via the brand's chosen DPP backend (atma.io, TrusTrace, EON, Authena or custom build). This dual function makes NFC the most cost-efficient approach. One tag, two critical capabilities.

faq.question: Where should the NFC DPP tag be placed on the product?
faq.answer: Placement depends on the product category: for textiles, embed in a care label or hang tag that stays with the garment; for electronics, place inside the battery compartment or on the product chassis; for batteries, integrate into the battery enclosure or label per EU 2023/1542 requirements; for cosmetics or spirits, use a tamper-evident NTAG 424 DNA TagTamper variant on the cap or seal; for packaging, embed in the packaging label or box. The tag must remain accessible throughout the product's useful life, including at end-of-life for recyclers. We advise on optimal placement for each product category.

faq.question: What is GS1 Digital Link 1.3 and why does my DPP need it?
faq.answer: GS1 Digital Link 1.3 (ISO/IEC 18975:2023) is the web-resolvable URL standard that carries product identifiers (GTIN + serial + batch + expiry) in a structure resolvable by any browser to a product master record. It is the de facto carrier format for DPP across NFC, QR and UHF RFID, mandated by the CIRPASS-2 reference architecture and adopted by the EU Battery Pass consortium. Your DPP NFC tag should encode a GS1 Digital Link URL pointing to your DPP backend, ensuring interoperability with other brands, retailers, repairers, recyclers and EU authorities.
